messages:
marie: Hey team — MediCore POC (Android) seeing intermittent SSE disconnects and lots of JSON.parse errors on client. Repro: open stream, after ~10–30s client throws 'Unexpected end of JSON input'. Can eng help debug? cc @sara

sara: Thanks — quick q: this is server-sent events (text/event-stream) from our hosted endpoint? Any proxy in front (APIGW, CDN)? Also paste a small dump of the raw SSE chunks and client error log pls.

marie: Yes SSE from the POC endpoint. Customer says they run requests thru their API gateway (unsure vendor). Here's the client error and a raw capture they sent:

Client log:
```
E/StreamParser: JSON.parse error: Unexpected end of JSON input
E/StreamParser: lastBytesReceived=256
```

Raw SSE chunks received by client (concatenated):
```
data: {"event":"update","payload":{"id":42,"note":"Patient rec\n\n
data: ords updated"}\n\n```

Looks like the JSON is being split mid-field resulting in invalid JSON on the client.

jordan: This reads like chunk boundary splitting/ buffering in the gateway or client parser not reassembling events. Two common fixes: ensure each SSE event ends with a double newline `\n\n` and flush after each event on server side; and disable proxy buffering. Can you confirm response headers and whether Transfer-Encoding: chunked is used?

sara: Also check for gzip/Content-Encoding — some CDNs buffer to recompress and that can break streaming. If you control nginx/apigw add `proxy_buffering off; proxy_cache off; chunked_transfer_encoding on;` and set `proxy_read_timeout` long. For FastAPI/uvicorn use `await response.flush()` after writing an event so it doesn't get coalesced.

marie: Customer provided gateway log snippet:
```
[2026-03-21T12:02:10Z] upstream response truncated after 18s idle (apigw timeout=18s)
[2026-03-21T12:02:11Z] client closed connection unexpectedly
```
They have a 18s idle timeout. Do we have any built-in keepalive/heartbeat they should enable from Redwood side?

sara: Yes — recommend emitting a comment-line heartbeat every 10–15s: `: keepalive\n\n` (SSE comment) — this keeps connection active without being parsed as data. Also add a newline-terminated framing for each event, e.g.
```
data: {"event":"update","payload":{...}}\n\n
```
Ensure server flushes after writing each event. Also set headers: `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, `Cache-Control: no-cache`, and `X-Accel-Buffering: no` (for nginx). If their gateway won't allow >18s idle, heartbeat frequency must be <18s.

jordan: For Android client parsing, confirm the SSE library handles multi-line events. Some libs expect entire event before JSON.parse; others do immediate parse per chunk. If they parse per chunk, switching to an aggregator on client side or using simple newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) could be a workaround. But NDJSON changes protocol, so prefer fixing streaming config.

marie: Got it. I'll tell them to try: 1) add SSE keepalive every 10s, 2) set headers and disable buffering, 3) ensure Transfer-Encoding: chunked, 4) flush per event.

ops-bot: :rotating_light: POC ticket #1234 escalated to eng-oncall — tag: `sse-streaming`

marie: Thanks all — scheduling quick 15m call with customer in 30m to push config changes. Will report back here. :thumbsup:
